about: Radio and intercom for chapter 2: Earth orbit, trans-lunar injection, transposition and docking, the coast. t = GET (seconds from liftoff). Original lines in the style of Apollo procedure; not quotes.

lines.text: Apollo, Houston. You're in a good orbit, ninety by ninety. You are go for orbit operations.
Roger, Houston. Helmets and gloves are coming off.
Look at that. The whole coastline, and not a cloud over it.
Apollo, Houston. All your systems look good from here. We'll have your TLI numbers for you shortly.
Apollo, Houston. One minute to loss of signal. We'll pick you up again over Carnarvon.
Sunrise coming up. It takes your breath away every time.
Apollo, Houston. You are go for TLI.
Roger, go for TLI. Thank you, Houston.
Ullage. Here we go again.
Apollo, Houston. We see ignition. Thrust is go.
You can see the Earth getting smaller already.
Shutdown.
Roger, shutdown. Apollo, you are on your way to the Moon.
Stand by for separation.
Sep.
The panels are gone. There she is.
Pitching around now.
I have the LM in the window. Coming in slow.
Ten metres. Five. Looking good.
Contact. Capture.
Hard dock. All twelve latches.
Apollo, Houston. You are go for LM extraction.
Springs are firing. We're free of the third stage.
Houston, the whole Earth fits in the window now. All of it, in one look.
We'd trade places with you for that view, Apollo.
Apollo, Houston. You're cleared to start passive thermal control.
Roger. Starting the barbecue roll.
Apollo, Houston. Good night from all of us. We'll keep an eye on things.
Good morning, Apollo. You're a hundred and eighty thousand kilometres out, and right on your path.
Apollo, Houston. Midcourse correction two is not required. Your trajectory is right on.
The Moon's a little bigger every time I look.
Apollo, Houston. In about eight hours you cross into the Moon's sphere of influence.
Apollo, the Moon's pull is now stronger than the Earth's. Welcome to lunar space.
